restrictions: The system is Windows 2000 build 2195 RTM with NO service pack, not Windows 2000 SP4: this verdict says nothing about SP4 (the plan, research R6, spike S1 and task T066 name SP4). The system DLLs read here are the RTM ones (kernel32.dll 5.0.2191.1, user32.dll 5.0.2180.1, msvcrt.dll 6.1.8637.0, dated 1999-12-07); SP4 replaces them with later builds, so the export tables confirmed here (tools/win2000_imports.json, confidence verified-on-vm) are those of RTM. Exports only grow from RTM to SP4, which makes a missing function on SP4 unlikely, but that was not checked.

Only one machine and one configuration, and an emulated one: VirtualBox 7.2.22 on a Windows 11 host, 1 vCPU, 168 MB RAM, VirtualBox Graphics Adapter 800x600x32 at 96 DPI, English (US) system with a French AZERTY keyboard layout for the user. No real hardware (physical chipset, display driver, input devices), no other Windows 2000 installation, language, edition (Server, Advanced Server) or hardware. Timings and memory are those of this VM: display_ms 3 to 13 ms and a constant peak_rss_kb of 1084 over the 20 '--probe' runs are not figures for real hardware.

Typing was exercised through the virtual keyboard of VirtualBox, not by a person: 'VBoxManage controlvm keyboardputstring Marie' assumes a US layout and the guest layout is French AZERTY, so it typed '?qrie' (the window then read 'Bonjour ?qrie', window-3-keyboardputstring.png); 'Marie' was then typed with the scancodes of the physical keys that give M, a, r, i, e on AZERTY (Home, Shift+End to select the prefilled text first) and the window read 'Marie' / 'Bonjour Marie' (window-4-typed-marie.png). The update delay of the greeting (User Story 1: within 1 second) was NOT measured: a screenshot is taken 1.5 s after the keys and shows the label already updated. No input method (IME), no clipboard paste, no typing of accented or non-Latin characters with the keyboard (those were only given through --probe-input), no mouse click on the field or on the close button (the window was closed with Alt+F4, scancodes).

The 1,000-character limit of the EDIT control was not tried with the keyboard on this system (no 1,100 keystrokes); text given by --probe-input bypasses that limit and is cut by the application itself (probe.cpp): the three vectors longer than 1,000 UTF-16 units (limit_4096_ascii, limit_4096_two_byte_chars, and in the extra battery 1,100 and 1,500 characters and 998 'a' + an emoji) were cut at 1,000 units without splitting a surrogate pair, as expected.

Glyph drawing: the probe checks the text of the greeting, and tools/run_vectors.py checks it character for character (15 of 15 reference vectors and 25 of 25 extra hard vectors), but this system's fonts do not draw everything. In a probe-mode window with 'Zoé Hélène çà 日本語 שלום 😀' (window-6-nonascii-probe.png, viewed by the author of the trial) the accented Latin letters are drawn correctly, the three CJK characters appear as three narrow missing-glyph boxes, the emoji (two UTF-16 units) as two such boxes, and the Hebrew letters are drawn (their order on screen was not checked). Nothing is garbled in the string itself.

No high contrast scheme, no DPI above 96 and no dark theme were tried: HKCU HighContrast Flags 126 (off), Win32_DisplayConfiguration.LogPixels 96, the AppsUseLightTheme value does not exist on this system. The Legacy UI took the skipped-feature path for two optional features, 'dpi-awareness' (user32.dll of this system does not export SetProcessDPIAware) and 'dark-mode' (no AppsUseLightTheme value), and displayed normally; 'high-contrast-query' (SystemParametersInfoW is exported) and 'peak-memory' (psapi.dll and GetProcessMemoryInfo exist) were available. The 4.5:1 contrast ratio of ui-contract item 2 was not measured (system colours are used).

Scope of the backend self-test run: loomora_selftest (core/tests/selftest.cpp) passes on this system, but only on this one RTM VM (see the first restriction), and it covers the greet vectors, loomora_abi_version and loomora_build_compiler only (loomora_is_eol and loomora_probe_record are not in selftest.cpp yet; the UI probe exercises them). History: the first attempt did NOT load (selftest-output.txt: the program built with <iostream> imported KERNEL32!GetThreadId and four Vista-only condition-variable functions through libgcc.a(gthr-win32-cond.o), the loader refused it with errorlevel 128 and no output); the fix was to remove <iostream> from selftest.cpp (output through std::fputs, no std::printf either because MinGW-w64 turns it into __mingw_vfprintf, which imports msvcrt _lock and _unlock that tools/win2000_imports.json does not list) and to link the GetThreadId shim of ADR 0002 into the selftest (core/tests/CMakeLists.txt). The fixed program (sha256 638449ff8e1aeb77a2905d5f5403b2843dc9f766c2f5a138b3bc0574403cdb89, 629,857 bytes) has 67 imports (kernel32 25, msvcrt 42), 0 outside the Windows 2000 SP4 allowlist and 0 not exported by the real DLLs of this system (selftest-noiostream-imports.txt, selftest-noiostream-vm-exports.txt); run from a .bat in the guest it printed 'all passed' and ended with errorlevel 0 (selftest-noiostream-vm-run.txt, .json). The control build without the shim still imports GetThreadId (not exported by this system's kernel32.dll) and is refused by the loader with errorlevel 128, so the shim is still needed.

The verdict covers the x86 executable out/windows-legacy/x86/loomora.exe (sha256 16e7859665c330a601f2d2afe15c8e955f64747c3533886a96de3a08f237494e) as built at commit d7f84de with MinGW-w64 GCC 13; it was started with CreateProcessW from a guest helper (tools/guest/runw.c, built with the same compiler), not by a double click in Explorer or from a command prompt typed by a person, and the guest processes were counted with WMI (Windows 2000 has no tasklist or taskkill). The helper's own run of the window without --probe used --nowait.

No procedure document exists yet for this trial (validation/procedures/windows.md is task T109), so the verdict carries no 'reproduction' path; the commands are in the 'notes' field and the driver script is part of the evidence.

Re-run after adr/0004-fallback-per-case.md (2026-11-13) with the same VM (RTM build 2195, no service pack): the executable of the evidence listed before this entry is sha256 16e7859665c330a601f2d2afe15c8e955f64747c3533886a96de3a08f237494e (694005 bytes); the x86 executable now built is sha256 67a695c888aa5deec4bba94638fcb8ba190314ee34ccecf8da1143a0447455a0 (696127 bytes; the MinGW linker stamps the build time, so a rebuild of the same source has another hash). RE-VERIFIED on the new one: 15 of 15 vectors (log not stored: a re-run), loomora_selftest 'all passed' with exit 0 (built with the Windows 2000 switches LOOMORA_AVOID_IOSTREAM and LOOMORA_TARGET_WIN2000), 112 of 112 imports and every allowlist function exported by the VM's DLLs, a screenshot of the new message font (validation/evidence/adr-0004/windows-2000-x86/vm-after-2-typed-marie.png; the screenshot before and the other files of this re-run are not stored, CLAUDE.md) (the look is the classic one; the font is the system message font, MS Sans Serif 8 pt). NOT re-run on the new executable: the two 10-run probe series, the memory cross-check, the non-ASCII glyph screenshot, the typing of 1,000 characters, the hard round-trip vectors; the statements of the earlier restrictions about them rest on the earlier executable. The manifest (Common Controls 6, supportedOS) is ignored by Windows 2000, so it was not exercised here.

notes: Windows 2000 trial of the Windows Legacy UI (x86 executable) in a VirtualBox VM, 2026-11-12, on the platform described in validation/platforms/windows-2000-x86.json (Windows 2000 build 2195, NO service pack). It covers the Windows 2000 part of T088, the Windows 2000 evidence of T094 and spike S1 / T066 for what it names; its deliverable record is validation/deliverables/windows-2000-x86-legacy.json (the x86 executable, written by tools/build.py windows legacy); it is the Legacy floor CANDIDATE for the Windows family only for what was actually tested on this VM (FR-005: the oldest platform on which the greeting really displays), and says nothing about SP4. What works on this system: the executable loads (112 of 112 imports exported), shows the window with the end-of-life banner, 'Bonjour Coucou', updates to 'Bonjour Marie' when typed with the virtual keyboard, takes the skipped-feature path for DPI awareness and dark mode, writes a valid probe line (20 of 20 runs, 15 + 25 of 40 vectors), exits cleanly after 2 s and with Alt+F4, and leaves no process. What does not: the guest's fonts do not draw CJK or emoji. The backend self-test loomora_selftest first did not load (Vista-only imports from libgcc's condition-variable code through <iostream>, first attempt kept in selftest-output.txt); after <iostream> was removed from core/tests/selftest.cpp and the ADR 0002 shim linked into it, it loads and prints 'all passed' with exit code 0 on this system (selftest-noiostream-vm-run.*). Commands (repository root, Windows 11 host, VM already running and logged on; LOOMORA_VM_NAME, LOOMORA_VM_USER and LOOMORA_VM_PASSWORD only needed if they differ from 'Windows 2000', 'name' and empty): 'wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 --cd <repo> -- python3 tools/build.py windows legacy', 'python tools/trials/windows-2000-x86/trial-driver.py' (facts, exports, runs, memory, gui, glyphs, selftest; the selftest step needs 'sh tools/guest/build_selftest.sh' and 'sh tools/trials/windows-2000-x86/loader-control.sh' in WSL first), 'wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 --cd <repo> -- sh tools/guest/build_selftest.sh' then 'python tools/trials/windows-2000-x86/selftest-driver.py' (the selftest after the fix; the selftest step of trial-driver.py is the first, failing attempt), 'python tools/run_vectors.py windows-2000-x86 legacy --evidence-dir validation/evidence/first-trial/windows-2000-x86/', and 'python tools/check_imports.py --verify-dlls <folder of the copied system DLLs>'. How the guest is driven: the old Guest Additions (6.1.18) do not pass command-line arguments to a guest program, and Windows Script Host 5.1 (WshShell.Run) converts the command line to the ANSI code page ('?' for every other character, measured) and expands %VARIABLES%, so each run copies cmdline.txt (UTF-16LE) and runs run.bat, which starts tools/guest/runw.c (kernel32 only, 5.5 KB); it reads the command line, calls CreateProcessW, waits and prints the exit status, the probe line and the leftover process count back through VBoxManage guestcontrol run. The guest folder created for the trial (C:\Documents and Settings\name\loomora-vectors) was deleted afterwards; the VM was left running as found, no snapshot was restored. The text files of this evidence folder keep their LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes marks them -text) because the verdict holds their sha256. ADR 0004 (2026-11-13): the Windows executables were rebuilt with the per-case fallback rule; the earlier evidence was produced with executable 16e78596...7494e and the rebuilt one 67a695c8...5a0 was re-verified (see the last restriction; the re-run is not stored except the capture of the new message font in validation/evidence/adr-0004/windows-2000-x86/); the 'measurements' of this record describe the earlier executable.
